plan: Jeremiah 49:1-6, 7-22, 23-27, 28-33; 2 Kings 24:5-7; 2 Chronicles 36:6-8; 2 Kings 24:8-9; 2 Chronicles 36:9; Jeremiah 22:24-30; Jeremiah 23:1-8, 9-32

readings.title: Malkam's Dispossession
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ěl will reclaim its inheritance, and Ammon will face exile and fear, yet a future restoration is promised.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 49:1] Concerning the Ammonites: Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Has Yisra’ěl no sons? Has he no heir? Why has Malkam taken possession of <dn>את</dn> Gaḏ, and his people dwell in its cities?</dq> [2] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when <dn>I</dn> shall sound a battle cry in Rabbah of the Ammonites. And it shall be a heap, a wasteland, and her villages shall be burned with fire. Then Yisra’ěl shall dispossess <dn>את</dn> those who dispossessed him,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] <dq>“Howl, O Ḥeshbon, for Ai is ravaged! Cry, daughters of Rabbah, gird on sackcloth! Lament and diligently search by the walls, for Malkam shall go into exile, with his priests and his heads.</dq> [4] <dq>“Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, O backsliding daughter who is trusting in her treasures, saying, ‘Who would come against me?’</dq> [5] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> fear upon you, from all those around you,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. <dq>“And you shall be driven out, each one straight ahead, with no one to bring home the wanderer.</dq> [6] <dq>“And after this <dn>I</dn> turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of the children of Ammon,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Fall of Prideful Edom
readings.subtitle: The wisdom of Těman has vanished; Edom will be made bare and desolate, its mighty men like women in labor.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 49:7] Concerning Eḏom: Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Is there no more wisdom in Těman? Has counsel been lost to those with understanding? Has their wisdom vanished?</dq> [8] <dq>“Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Deḏan! For <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>את</dn> the calamity of Ěsav upon him, <dn>את</dn> the time that <dn>I</dn> shall punish him.</dq> [9] <dq>“If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? Even thieves by night would destroy only until they had enough!</dq> [10] <dq>“But as for <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> Ěsav bare. <dn>I</dn> shall uncover <dn>את</dn> his hiding places, so that he is unable to conceal himself. <dn>His</dn> seed is ravaged, his brothers and his neighbours, and he is no more.</dq> [11] <dq>“Leave your fatherless children, let <dn>Me</dn> keep them alive. And let your widows trust in <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [12] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, those whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have certainly drunk. And are you the one to go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but certainly drink of it.</dq> [13] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have sworn by <dn>Myself</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that Botsrah is to become a ruin, a reproach, a waste, and a curse, and all its cities become everlasting wastes.”</dq> [14] <dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> a report from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and an envoy has been sent to the nations, <dq>“Gather together, come against her, and rise up to battle!</dq> [15] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> shall make you small among nations, despised among men.</dq> [16] <dq>“The dread for you, the pride of your heart, has deceived you, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, holding the height of the hill! Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there <dn>I</dn> bring you down,”</dq> declares the Master. [17] <dq>“And Eḏom shall be a ruin, everyone who passes by it is astonished and whistles at all its plagues.</dq> [18] <dq>“As in the overthrow of Seḏom and Amorah and their neighbouring cities,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“No one shall dwell there, nor would a son of man sojourn in it.</dq> [19] <dq>“See, he comes up like a lion from the Yarděn jungle against the home of the strong. But in an instant <dn>I</dn> shall make him run away from her. And who is the Chosen One, to appoint over her? For who is like <dn>Me</dn>? And who summons <dn>Me</dn>? And who is that Shepherd who stands before <dn>Me</dn>?”</dq> [20] Therefore hear <dn>את</dn> the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> has counselled concerning Eḏom, and <dn>את</dn> the purposes <dn>He</dn> has purposed concerning the inhabitants of Těman: the least of the flock shall drag them away! <dn>He</dn> shall make their pasture a waste before them! [21] The earth shall be shaken at the noise of their fall. There is an outcry! Its noise is heard at the Sea of Reeds. [22] See, like an eagle he flies up, and spreads his wings over Botsrah. And the heart of the mighty men of Eḏom in that day shall be like the heart of a woman in her pain.

readings.title: Damascus Becomes Feeble
readings.subtitle: The cities of Ḥamath and Arpaḏ are shamed, and Dammeseq is seized with trembling and pain.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 49:23] Concerning Dammeseq: “Ḥamath and Arpaḏ have been put to shame, for they have heard an evil report. They have been melted in anxiety, like the sea, unable to rest. [24] “Dammeseq has become feeble, she has turned to flee, and trembling has taken hold of her. Distress and pain have seized her like a woman in labour. [25] “How is the city of praise deserted, the city of <dn>My</dn> joy! [26] <dq>“Therefore her young men fall in her streets, and all the men of battle are cut off in that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [27] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall kindle a fire in the wall of Dammeseq, and it shall consume <dn>את</dn> the palaces of Ben-Haḏaḏ.”</dq>

readings.title: The Ravaging of the Men of the East
readings.subtitle: Nebuchadnezzar will plunder the tents and flocks of the nation that dwells at ease, scattering them to the winds.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 49:28] To Qěḏar and to the reigns of Ḥatsor, which Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel struck: Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Arise, go up to Qěḏar, and ravage the men of the East!</dq> [29] <dq>“Their tents and their flocks, their curtains and all their vessels shall be taken. And they shall take away <dn>את</dn> their camels for themselves. And they shall cry out to them, ‘Fear is on every side!’</dq> [30] <dq>“Flee, go away! Dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Ḥatsor!”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“For Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel has taken counsel against you, and has devised a plan against you.</dq> [31] <dq>“Arise, go up to the nation at ease that dwells safely,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“It has no gates or bars, they dwell alone.</dq> [32] <dq>“And their camels shall become plunder, and their large herds booty. And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter them to all winds, <dn>את</dn> those who cut off the corner, and bring <dn>את</dn> their calamity from all its sides,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [33] <dq>"Ḥatsor shall be a habitation for jackals, a desert forever. No one dwells there, nor does son of man sojourn in it.”</dq>

readings.title: The Death of Jehoiakim
readings.subtitle: Jehoiakim sleeps with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin reigns in his place as Babylon's power grows.
readings.text: [2 Kings 24:5] And the rest of the acts of Yehoyaqim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [6] So Yehoyaqim slept with his fathers. And Yehoyaḵin his son reigned in his place. [7] And the sovereign of Mitsrayim did not come out of his land again, for the sovereign of Baḇel had taken <dn>את</dn> all that belonged to the sovereign of Mitsrayim from the wadi of Mitsrayim to the River Euphrates.

readings.title: Jehoiachin's Evil Reign
readings.subtitle: At eighteen years old, Jehoiachin reigns for three months, doing evil in the sight of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Kings 24:8] Yehoyaḵin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim three new moons. And his mother’s name was Neḥushta the daughter of Elnathan of Yerushalayim. [9] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his father did.

readings.section: Prophecies Against the Kings of Judah
readings.title: The Signet Ring Cast Off
readings.subtitle: Though he were a signet on God's right hand, Coniah will be hurled into exile and written down as childless.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:24] <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> live,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“though Konyahu son of Yehoyaqim, sovereign of Yehuḏah, were the signet on <dn>My</dn> right hand, <dn>I</dn> would still pull you off from there;</dq> [25] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> shall give you into the hand of those who seek <dn>את</dn> your life, and into the hand of those whose face you fear, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel and the hand of the Kasdim.</dq> [26] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall hurl <dn>את</dn> you out, and <dn>את</dn> your mother who bore you, into another land where you were not born, and there you shall die.</dq> [27] <dq>“But they shall not return to the land to which their being yearns to return.</dq> [28] “Is this man Konyahu a despised broken pot, or an undesirable vessel? Why are they hurled out, he and his descendants, and cast into a land which they do not know? [29] “O land, land, land! Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [30] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Write <dn>את</dn> this man down as childless, a strong man who is not to prosper in his days, for none of his descendants shall prosper, sitting on the throne of Daviḏ, or rule any more in Yehuḏah.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Righteous Branch of David
readings.subtitle: After punishing the evil shepherds, YeHoVaH will gather His flock and raise up a righteous King, 'YeHoVaH our Righteousness'.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 23:1] <dq>“Woe to the shepherds destroying and scattering the sheep of <dn>My</dn> pasture!”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl against the shepherds who feed <dn>My</dn> people, <dq>“You have scattered <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> flock, driven them away, and have not tended them. See, <dn>I</dn> am punishing you for <dn>את</dn> the evil of your deeds,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall gather <dn>את</dn> the remnant of <dn>My</dn> flock out of all the lands where <dn>I</dn> have driven them, and shall bring them back to their fold. And they shall bear and increase.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall raise up shepherds over them, and they shall feed them. And they shall fear no more, nor be discouraged, nor shall they be lacking,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [5] <dq>“See, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when <dn>I</dn> shall raise for Daviḏ a Branch of righteousness, and a Sovereign shall reign and act wisely, and shall do right-ruling and righteousness in the earth.</dq> [6] <dq>“In <dn>His</dn> days Yehuḏah shall be saved, and Yisra’ěl dwell safely. And this is <dn>His</dn> Name whereby <dn>He</dn> shall be called: ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our Righteousness.’</dq> [7] <dq>“Therefore, see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when they shall say no more, ‘As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives who brought up the children of Yisra’ěl out of the land of Mitsrayim,’</dq> [8] <dq>but, ‘As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives who brought up and led the seed of the house of Yisra’ěl out of the land of the north and from all the lands where <dn>I</dn> had driven them.’ And they shall dwell on their own soil.”</dq>

readings.title: A Land Filled with Adulterers
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah's heart is broken over the defiled prophets and priests who lead the people astray with visions of their own hearts.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 23:9] My heart within me is broken because of the prophets; all my bones shake. I am like a drunken man, and like a man overcome by wine, because of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and because of <dn>His</dn> set-apart words. [10] For the land is filled with adulterers; for the land mourns because of a curse. The pastures of the wilderness are dried up. And their course is evil, and their might is not right. [11] <dq>“For both prophet and priest have become defiled. Even in <dn>My</dn> house <dn>I</dn> have found <dn>את</dn> their evil,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [12] <dq>“Therefore their way is to them like slippery ways in the dark. They are driven on and they shall fall in them. For <dn>I</dn> bring <dn>את</dn> evil on them, <dn>את</dn> the year of their punishment,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have seen folly in the prophets of Shomeron: they prophesied by Ba‛al and led <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl astray.</dq> [14] <dq>“And among the prophets of Yerushalayim <dn>I</dn> have seen a horrible matter: committing adultery and walking in falsehood. And they strengthen the hands of evil ones, so that no one turns back from his evil. All of them are like Seḏom to <dn>Me</dn>, and her inhabitants like Amorah.</dq> [15] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts concerning the prophets, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am making them eat wormwood, and shall make them drink <dn>את</dn> poisoned water. For defilement has gone out into all the land from the prophets of Yerushalayim.’ ”</dq> [16] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you, they lead you astray. They speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>“They keep on saying to those who despise <dn>Me</dn>, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said you shall have peace.’ And to all who walk according to the stubbornness of their own heart they say, ‘No evil comes upon you.’ ”</dq> [18] For who has stood in the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and has seen and heard <dn>His</dn> word? Who has listened to <dn>His</dn> word and obeyed it? [19] See, a storm of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go forth in a rage, a whirling storm! It whirls on the head of the wrong. [20] The displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall not turn back until <dn>He</dn> has done and established the purposes of <dn>His</dn> heart. In the latter days you shall understand it perfectly. [21] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> did not send these prophets, yet they ran. <dn>I</dn> have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.</dq> [22] <dq>“But if they had stood in <dn>My</dn> counsel, then they would have let <dn>My</dn> people hear <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Words, and they would have turned them from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.</dq>

readings.subsection: The True Word vs. False Dreams
readings.title: Chaff to the Wheat
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH, who fills heaven and earth, declares His Word is like fire and a hammer, and He is against the prophets of false dreams.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 23:23] <dq>“Am <dn>I</dn> an <dn>Elohim</dn> close by,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and not an <dn>Elohim</dn> afar off?</dq> [24] <dq>“If anyone is hidden in secret places, would <dn>I</dn> not see him?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Do <dn>I</dn> not fill <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> earth?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [25] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> what the prophets have said who prophesy falsehood in <dn>My</dn> Name, saying, ‘<dn>I</dn> have dreamed, <dn>I</dn> have dreamed!’</dq> [26] <dq>“Till when shall it be in the heart of the prophets? – the prophets of falsehood and prophets of the deceit of their own heart,</dq> [27] <dq>who try to make <dn>My</dn> people forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name by their dreams which everyone relates to his neighbour, as their fathers forgot <dn>My</dn> Name for Ba‛al.</dq> [28] <dq>“The prophet who has a dream, let him relate the dream, and he who has <dn>My</dn> Word, let him speak <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Word in truth. What is the chaff to the wheat?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [29] <dq>“Is not <dn>My</dn> Word like a fire?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and like a hammer that shatters a rock?</dq> [30] <dq>“Therefore see, <dn>I</dn> am against the prophets,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“who steal <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Words every one from his neighbour.</dq> [31] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against the prophets,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“who use their tongues and say, ‘<dn>He</dn> declares.’</dq> [32] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against those who prophesy false dreams,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and relate them, and lead <dn>My</dn> people astray by their falsehoods and by their reckless boasting. But <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> did not send them nor have <dn>I</dn> commanded them. And they do not profit <dn>את</dn> this people at all,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
